elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "IBM may assign this Agreement without MSL's approval to an affiliate of IBM ..." — a direct no-approval permission for Customer affiliate transfers.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence continues "... or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets" without MSL's approval, tracking the checklist triggers verbatim.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Retained operative text: "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM." Also reinforced by the retained mutual first sentence.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "IBM's approval of any other assignment by MSL shall not be unreasonably withheld," which, read with the retained Related-Company sentence ("not be unreasonably withheld or delayed"), covers MSL assignments generally.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "MSL may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of IBM" — an unconditional prohibition, not subject to a consent cure.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "no change of control of IBM shall give MSL any right to terminate this Agreement"; no contrary change-of-control termination right appears in the cited text.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only IBM receives a successor transfer right; MSL remains barred ("MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties ... without prior written approval by IBM"). Section 16.5 only obliges an MSL acquirer to assume the Agreement; it grants MSL no assignment right.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted permission contains no notice obligation; the only notice duty is MSL's immediate notice of a sale/merger under the retained 16.5 sentence, which is not a successor-assignment notice condition.
The insertion creates a standing no-consent exception for IBM affiliate transfers (a non-successor exception), which defeats the fallback requirement that all other assignments run through consent.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The reasonableness standard is one-directional: it governs only "any other assignment by MSL." Any IBM assignment outside the affiliate/successor carve-out still needs MSL's "prior written approval" with no reasonableness qualifier.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative language: the two-sentence insertion supplies the Customer affiliate and merger/acquisition/substantially-all-assets carve-outs, the competitor bar, the reasonableness standard on IBM's approval of MSL assignments, and the express no-change-of-control-termination confirmation, while the retained sentence "MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM" already carries the Vendor-consent element.

Fallback is incomplete (no MSL successor right, no written-notice condition, a retained no-consent affiliate exception, and no mutual reasonableness standard), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation since the as-drafted clause failed the fallback on material terms.

Minimality holds: nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased, the favourable retained language (mutual approval sentence, MSL Related Company reasonableness, subcontractor disclosure, 16.5 successor-assumption warranty) survives intact, and the drafter used a direct "without MSL's approval" permission rather than a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause. No survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure was added.

Intent is preserved: the added permission operates as a specific exception to the retained general "Neither Party may assign ... without prior written approval" sentence rather than contradicting it, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Minor drafting point (not a defect requiring repair): "any other assignment by MSL" sits alongside the retained MSL Related Company consent sentence, so consider confirming that the competitor prohibition overrides a Related Company transfer to an IBM competitor if that risk is live.
